title: Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a broad, experimentally grounded account of how important noncoding DNA elements and poorly understood proteins contribute to biological processes. For each studied element or protein, it would connect a controlled perturbation to a molecular mechanism and a relevant phenotype, while identifying the cell types and conditions in which that relationship holds. The supplied atlas illustrates a route toward this capability through large-scale gene perturbation, morphological profiling and selected mechanistic follow-up.

Conceptual synthesis. Assigning function requires keeping several questions distinct. Sequence conservation concerns evolutionary history and constraint. Biochemical activity describes a measurable molecular action. A cellular phenotype records an observable consequence under particular experimental conditions. A mechanistic explanation connects an intervention to the processes producing that consequence. These forms of evidence can reinforce one another, but each answers a different question. The supplied review supports the distinction between phenotypic profiling and mechanistic interpretation, while the evolutionary distinctions require additional evidence.

Scope synthesis. The intended map would record context dependence, uncertainty and cases with no detected effect alongside positive findings. Coverage would be defined by an explicit sampling frame for conserved noncoding elements, poorly characterized proteins, cell types and conditions. The goal leaves open how much genomic sequence has a selected function. A null result in a particular assay leaves several possibilities, including an untested context, an insensitive measurement or an element with no relevant function under the tested conditions.

significance.text: At representative scale, reproducible links from perturbations through mechanisms to phenotypes would make many descriptive genomic and proteomic observations experimentally interpretable. Researchers could investigate which components drive a process, how their effects arise and where those effects change with biological context. The atlas supplies a concrete example of this progression through follow-up experiments supporting a role for TMEM251/LYSET in lysosomal enzyme trafficking through the mannose-6-phosphate system. Extending such interpretation across many poorly characterized proteins and noncoding elements is the proposed advance.

Conditional impact synthesis. A sufficiently broad map could improve the interpretation of disease-associated observations, suggest diagnostic hypotheses and provide starting points for biological engineering. It could also help prioritize experiments by identifying likely pathways, dependencies and context-specific effects. Clinical diagnosis, therapeutic targeting and effective treatments would each require further validation of relevance, intervention feasibility and outcomes.

Impact boundary synthesis. Functional annotation remains conditional on the biological system and measurements used. An element or protein can participate in several processes, and an experimentally established role in one setting leaves its other roles open. The revolutionary capability would be systematic access to causal explanations across a documented range of contexts. Historical ranking, universal coverage and clinical benefit remain separate questions.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability still required by this proposal is scalable movement from perturbation signatures to reproducible causal mechanisms across representative human biological contexts. The atlas demonstrates the scale possible for morphology-based screening, while emphasizing the need for targeted experiments to interpret individual features biologically. Its comparisons also show that measured perturbation effects depend on environment. For example, processes associated with iron-sulfur cluster assembly, mitochondrial RNA metabolism and mitochondrial transcription were selectively enriched in the DMEM screen.

Engineering synthesis. Broad coverage would require perturbations, measurements and follow-up experiments that work across diverse cell types, cell states and environments. Experiments must distinguish direct consequences from downstream responses and account for interactions that can mask or modify an effect. Scaling the initial screen is only one component. Mechanistic follow-up, comparison across contexts and independent replication must also become sufficiently systematic to support the intended breadth.

Noncoding-function synthesis. For noncoding elements, the proposed capability must connect perturbing a sequence to the molecular process it influences and to the resulting phenotype. Conservation can help define a sampling frame, but assigning selected evolutionary function requires appropriate evolutionary evidence. The supplied atlas supplies gene-knockout evidence and selected protein-function interpretation. The noncoding and evolutionary components therefore require a separate experimental and evidentiary foundation.

current_state.text: Ramezani, Weisbart and colleagues published A genome-wide atlas of human cell morphology online on January 27, 2025, with DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02537-7. The abstract on printed page 621 reports CRISPR–Cas9 knockout maps covering more than 20,000 genes and more than 30 million cells. These figures describe the study's reported screening scale. They do not measure the number of genes assigned a complete molecular mechanism.

The study describes three maps spanning two cancer cell lines, HeLa and A549, with HeLa examined in two media. Its environmental comparisons demonstrate that perturbation-associated effects can change with growth conditions. This is substantial context-sensitive screening within a limited experimental scope. Representative coverage of human tissues, developmental states and physiological conditions remains outside the demonstrated scope described in the supplied review.

Morphological features provide hypotheses for functional investigation, and the paper explicitly calls for targeted follow-up to establish their biological interpretation. Selected experiments support a role for TMEM251/LYSET in lysosomal enzyme trafficking through the mannose-6-phosphate system. This supplies a mechanistic example within the atlas. The reported gene-targeting work leaves broad causal annotation of conserved noncoding elements and mechanisms for every screened protein unestablished.

The supplied review verified the article's identity and evaluated readable extracted text. That text was truncated during Methods, some pages lacked extractable text, and an extraction warning reported skipped form content after an invocation limit. Figures and raw data were not independently inspected in that review. The quantitative and mechanistic statements above therefore reflect the reported paper as assessed through partial text access.

Evidence-coverage limitation. The supplied search record is empty. This record establishes a documented January 2025 achievement, while the field's subsequent progress through November 2026 remains unassessed. The available material consequently cannot settle whether later work has achieved broader portions of the proposed capability.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Establish reproducible causal roles for a large, transparently sampled set of conserved noncoding elements and poorly characterized proteins across independently selected human cell types and conditions. Before evaluation, specify the sampling frame, coverage targets, context selection, reproducibility thresholds and criteria for causal and mechanistic validation. The numerical targets and acceptable evidence levels would need explicit justification. They are proposed evaluation choices whose values remain open.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible causal roles across prespecified elements, proteins and cellular contexts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation. For each claimed role, connect the perturbation to a relevant molecular mechanism and phenotype using suitable controls and corroborating experiments. Where feasible, test whether restoring the perturbed component or using an independent intervention reproduces the expected causal relationship. Selected findings should be repeated by independent investigators, with enough methodological detail and accessible data to assess the result.
completion_criteria.label: Each claimed role experimentally links perturbation, molecular mechanism and phenotype

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting and boundaries. Report null, ambiguous and context-dependent results, including the sensitivity and limitations of the assays. Separate measured phenotypic effects, supported mechanisms and evolutionary interpretations in the reported evidence. Assess performance across the prespecified sampling frame and disclose gaps in coverage. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth over that frame, with generalization to additional contexts remaining an empirical question.
completion_criteria.label: Reported outcomes distinguish evidence levels and disclose assay and coverage limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis. BIO-03, Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts, shares the need to understand context-dependent consequences of genomic perturbations. BIO-14 centers on experimentally established causal roles and mechanisms. BIO-03 centers on prospective prediction of the effects of genome changes. Mechanistic annotations could inform prediction, and predictive discrepancies could motivate functional experiments. This comparison uses the supplied roster title and candidate description because the full BIO-03 record was unavailable.

Roster-based synthesis. BIO-04, Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell, could use causal functional maps to constrain and test cellular models. Its deliverable is an integrated predictive representation of cellular behavior, while BIO-14 produces experimentally grounded explanations for particular elements and proteins across defined contexts. BIO-10, Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale, concerns measurement capabilities that could reveal mechanisms and improve readouts for BIO-14. Observations would still require causal experiments to establish the proposed functional relationships.

Roster-based synthesis. BIO-15, Deliver programmable genome editors selectively to diverse cells in the body, could expand which cell populations can be perturbed for functional studies. Its central challenge is selective delivery, while BIO-14 requires interpretation and validation of biological consequences. BIO-05, Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes, overlaps where understanding protein mechanisms informs design. BIO-05 evaluates the creation of specified catalytic functions, and BIO-14 evaluates causal roles of existing biological components.

Roster-based synthesis. BIO-09, Observe and causally test whole-brain computation at cellular resolution, and BIO-13, Establish the physical mechanisms that store and retrieve a long-term memory, could draw on functional annotations of proteins and regulatory elements involved in neural processes. Their completion criteria concern brain computation and memory mechanisms at additional levels of organization. Broad molecular annotation alone would leave those system-level demonstrations outstanding.

change_log.change: Preserved BIO-14's identity and expanded the explanation of causal function, mechanism and context-dependent phenotype.
change_log.reason: The research and review jointly support a functional-biology goal extending beyond large-scale profiling.

change_log.change: Retained the distinctions among conservation, biochemical activity, phenotype and mechanism, while labeling the broader evolutionary interpretation as synthesis.
change_log.reason: The supplied atlas supports context dependence and mechanistic follow-up, but supplies insufficient evolutionary evidence to substantiate every part of the original problem statement.

change_log.change: Reframed the claim about sequence lacking selected function as an open question and explained the limited interpretation of an undetected phenotype.
change_log.reason: The evidence neither establishes that evolutionary assertion nor permits absence of a measured effect to establish absence of function.

change_log.change: Preserved the reported totals of more than 20,000 genes and more than 30 million cells, and added the three-map, two-cell-line scope.
change_log.reason: The review verifies the abstract totals and provides experimental context necessary to interpret their breadth.

change_log.change: Integrated the environmental comparison and TMEM251/LYSET follow-up into the relevant scientific sections.
change_log.reason: These findings explain context dependence and demonstrate a concrete progression from profiling to supported mechanistic interpretation.

change_log.change: Added prespecified sampling, coverage and validation criteria to the proposed completion milestone.
change_log.reason: These choices make representative scale and reproducibility assessable while keeping proposed criteria distinct from established standards.

change_log.change: Preserved partial-access, extraction and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: The review relied on truncated extracted text, and the empty search record cannot establish the field's status through November 2026.

change_log.change: Expanded roster-based connections and retained the distinction from BIO-03.
change_log.reason: The supplied roster supports conceptual comparisons, while the unavailable full records limit entry-specific verification.

unresolved_issues: No quantitative sampling frame, coverage target or reproducibility threshold has been selected for the proposed milestone.
The appropriate evidence requirements for noncoding regulatory mechanisms and selected evolutionary function remain to be specified.
The supplied evidence does not establish how much genomic sequence lacks selected function or distinguish the possible explanations for individual null results.
Progress after the documented January 2025 publication remains unassessed because the supplied search record is empty.
Incomplete PDF extraction and the absence of independent figure or raw-data inspection limit the supplied review's coverage.
The full BIO-03 record and other roster entries were unavailable, so overlap assessments remain based on their supplied titles and the candidate's stated distinction.

brief.title: Knowing what overlooked DNA and proteins do
possible: Researchers could explain how poorly understood proteins and noncoding DNA—DNA that does not encode proteins—affect cells. They could trace what happens when a component is changed, how it produces that effect, and which cell types and conditions make a difference.
why: This would turn lists of biological components into explanations of how cells work. Researchers could identify what drives a process, interpret disease-associated changes and choose more informative experiments. The resulting map could also provide starting points for diagnosis and biological engineering.

sources.who: Meraj Ramezani, Erin Weisbart and colleagues
sources.showed: They measured changes in cell appearance after disabling more than 20,000 genes. Follow-up experiments linked a poorly understood protein to the delivery of enzymes to cells’ recycling compartments.
sources.quote:
Using this atlas, we identify the poorly 
characterized disease-associated TMEM251/LYSET as a Golgi-resident 
transmembrane protein essential for mannose-6-phosphate-dependent 
trafficking of lysosomal enzymes.
sources.cited_for: Large-scale screening can reveal candidate functions and lead to a detailed explanation for a selected protein.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish mechanisms for every screened protein or broad functions for noncoding DNA across human tissues.

sources.who: Tyler Fair, Bryan J Pavlovic and colleagues
sources.showed: They tested DNA sequences retained in chimpanzees but lost in humans. In chimpanzee stem cells, they identified 20 such regions that control gene activity.
sources.quote: we discovered 20 hDels controlling gene expression.
sources.cited_for: Changing noncoding DNA in its original location can reveal effects on gene activity and cell growth.
sources.not_established: Findings in chimpanzee stem cells do not establish causal roles across representative human cell types and conditions.

sources.who: Florence M Chardon, Troy A McDiarmid and colleagues
sources.showed: They activated candidate DNA switches and measured gene activity in cancer cells and laboratory-grown neurons. Individual switches often responded in only one cell type.
sources.quote: For enhancers in particular, the upregulatory potential of individual gRNAs was consistently restricted to one cell type
sources.cited_for: Tests of DNA switches can identify the genes they control and reveal dependence on cell type.
sources.not_established: Artificial activation does not establish a switch’s full natural role, its molecular mechanism or its effects across human tissues.

sources.who: Naomi M. Pacalin, Zachary Steinhart and colleagues
sources.showed: They built a system that activates one DNA location while repressing another. It revealed interactions between gene regulators and helped explain how DNA switches control a gene in immune cells.
sources.quote:
Finally, multiple independent gRNAs targeting the same 
gene had concordant impacts on target gene expression (Extended 
Data Fig. 3c).
sources.cited_for: Paired interventions can help explain how regulatory components interact and how their effects depend on cellular context.
sources.not_established: Selected regulatory interactions do not establish mechanisms across a representative set of noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins.

sources.who: C. C.-S. Hsiung, C. M. Wilson and colleagues
sources.showed: They engineered a tool that represses several DNA locations together. In human cells, it identified DNA switches and tested how combinations of them affect gene activity.
sources.quote:
Using multiAsCas12a-KRAB, we discover 
enhancer elements and dissect the combinatorial function of cis-regulatory 
elements in human cells.
sources.cited_for: Testing combinations can reveal interactions that experiments on isolated components may miss.
sources.not_established: A tool for testing combinations does not itself provide broad, independently reproduced explanations of biological function.

shown: Ramezani, Weisbart and colleagues measured cell appearance after gene disruption at genome scale and explained a selected protein’s role in enzyme delivery. Other teams have linked particular noncoding regions to gene activity and tested interactions among DNA switches.

These studies show that experiments can move from finding an effect to explaining selected functions. They also show that effects depend on cell type and growth conditions. Broad coverage of human biology remains beyond these demonstrations.
missing: A representative set of noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins still needs reproducible causal explanations across human cells and conditions.
Mechanistic follow-up must scale alongside screening, distinguishing direct effects from downstream responses and interactions.
Independent teams must reproduce selected findings, with clear accounts of undetected effects, measurement sensitivity and coverage gaps.

milestones.label: Causal roles repeat across a predefined biological sample
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to reproduce causal roles across a large, predefined sample of elements, proteins and human cellular contexts, using justified criteria. This would establish breadth beyond selected examples.

milestones.label: Each role connects an intervention to mechanism and outcome
milestones.explanation: Each claimed role would need controlled experiments linking a change to a molecular process and an observable effect, with independent replication of selected findings. This would turn screening signals into causal explanations.

milestones.label: Results distinguish effects, explanations and limits
milestones.explanation: Reports would have to include absent, ambiguous and context-dependent effects, separate observations from mechanisms and evolutionary claims, and disclose test sensitivity and coverage gaps. This would define how far the map applies.

uncertain: The required breadth of sampling and the thresholds for reproducibility and mechanistic support remain undecided.
Evidence standards for noncoding regulation and for functions maintained by natural selection still need definition.
An undetected effect may reflect an untested context, an insensitive measurement or no relevant function under the tested conditions.
